panels.title: Big questions
points: Why might two deals that cost the same be treated so differently in Islam?

panels.title: Islamic foundation
panels.text: Islamic note: riba (رِبَا) is forbidden (Qur'an 2:275: Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba). Islamic finance uses partnership (mushārakah, مُشَارَكَة) and cost-plus sale (murābaḥah, مُرَابَحَة) instead. We learn how interest works as knowledge of the wider economy, never as something to take.

keywords.def: رِبَا: an increase charged for lending money, forbidden in Islam
مُرَابَحَة: a cost-plus sale at a fixed agreed price
مُشَارَكَة: a partnership sharing profit as agreed and loss by capital
interest on the original amount only

panels.title: Saving and borrowing without riba: halal finance
points: Riba: an increase charged for lending money
Trade with an agreed profit is permitted
The bank buys the item, then sells at an agreed price
